summary: Validated security remediation (JWT auth) on Webora backend. All 23 targeted tests passed: (a) bogus 'Bearer faketoken' rejected on 12 admin/contract endpoints, (b) tokens forged with the OLD hardcoded secret rejected on GET /api/applications/ and DELETE /api/applications/{id}, (c) applicant tokens forbidden (403) on admin endpoints, (d) legit admin flow works (GET /applications/, GET /contracts/ both 200), (e) legit applicant flow still works (GET /applications/status, /my-contract both 200), (f) BOLA fixed: applicant CANNOT read/download another applicant's contract (403). JWT_SECRET_KEY is loaded from backend/.env and auth.py fails-closed when missing.
critical_code_review_comments: utils/auth.py is correctly fail-closed on missing JWT_SECRET_KEY — good.
routes/applications.py: _require_admin() is defined at line 871 but used starting at line 217; works due to Python late binding, but consider moving helpers to top of file for readability.
routes/contracts.py: BOLA checks are consistent — compare payload['sub'] to contract['employee_email'] with admin bypass. Correct.

Several endpoints (status, my-contract, sign-contract, skip-contract, download-contract, upload verification) still inline the 'Bearer' parse + decode instead of using _verify_token helper — works but repeats logic. DRY opportunity, non-blocking.
Applications.py file is >1200 lines — should be split into applicants/, admin/, contracts_templates/ modules (file-size guideline).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Security remediation validated end-to-end. Regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_security_auth_remediation.py covers all endpoints from the review request. Run with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exported. PyJWT is used to craft old-secret tokens; python-jose is the app's runtime lib.
rca of the issue: Original incident RCA (confirmed by code inspection + tests): (1) utils/auth.py had SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('JWT_SECRET_KEY', '<hardcoded>') so if env was missing, every deployment shared the same signing secret — attacker could forge admin JWTs. (2) Many admin endpoints only checked `authorization.startswith('Bearer ')` without decoding the token or verifying role=='admin'. (3) /api/contracts/{id} did not restrict access based on employee_email, enabling BOLA. Fix validated: fail-closed secret load, _require_admin() enforced (decode + role check), ownership check on contract read/download/sign.
